propositions: The _recall_false_accept function computes specificity (true-negative rate, higher-is-better) but the gating comparisons treat it as an error rate (lower-is-better), inverting the criterion direction

Both consumption sites at parity.py:125 and parity.py:252 fail candidates for improvements in false-firing accuracy and reject all runs as exceeding the 0.10 ceiling, because the metric computation is inverted relative to its consumption

The recorded frontier slot of the live Bedrock provider-parity run was incorrectly failed on false-accept regression when Bedrock actually showed a 14.3 percentage-point improvement in false-positive rate over Anthropic

Correcting the false_accept computation from not-blocked/safe to blocked/safe aligns parity.py with the existing canonical definition in evals/eval.py, the plan-review-gate docs, and the container eval tolerances

The fidelity_spot_eval.py fixture contradicted itself by labelling conflict blocks as advisory (safe) while comments stated they must never be shipped, which was only survivable with the inverted metric
